summary: ITEM 1 IS REFUTED AND THEN COMPLETED. The false clause is NOT in src/opt/api.py and never was: x_spine FILED it as a patch to land, z_spine INTERCEPTED it ("DO NOT LAND x_spine's version") and filed a corrected patch, and neither ever landed -- so nothing travelled. Verified three ways on the current tree: `git status --porcelain` lists neither src/opt/api.py nor src/spine/derive.py as modified this run; grep for every fragment of the clause ('missed every deficit', 'smaller than accum', 'flooring') over src/, docs/ and tests/ returns nothing; and counters() had no resume guard at all -- the line before `due = derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(...)` was the divisor comment. So I landed z_spine's CORRECTED guard, which is what the file was actually owed, with every clause re-derived rather than copied: load_state stamps the base FROM st.n_backward AFTER the restore (opt/api.py:2158) and scaled_backward only adds U.Backwards(1) (opt/api.py:944), both read before quoting. ITEM 2: all three asymmetries re-measured on the live tree, and TWO ARE ACCIDENTAL AND ONE IS DELIBERATE. (1) The rate end took anything int() takes -- flush_period(Steps(20000), 16.9) = Flushes(1250) for a rate 6% off, '16' the same for a value that never went through Lever.coerce, and nan/inf left as ValueError/OverflowError, escaping the family's own exception type -- the exact defect z_spine repaired one layer down in units.Clock.convert on 2026-09-04. All six rate ends are now `type(rate) is not int`, the exact-type shape the clock end always had; units.Clock.convert's fractional `per` is untouched and still tested. (2) THE COUNT END WAS WIDER THAN FILED AND LIVE. Three behaviours for one situation: opt_steps_from_backwards refused, run_windows_from_epochs passed a negative through, and flush_period, flush_period_windows and opt_steps_from_windows FLOORED it to one -- the tightest cadence and the shortest horizon that exist. Two of those were reachable at BUILD time through spine/assemble.py::COUPLINGS and I measured them: FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-500 built FAB.d_manage_period=Flushes(1) and CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=-20000 built FAB.d_cap_lift_period and TOK.d_cap_lift_period=Flushes(1), so a negative lever became a management pass and a capacity valve firing every flush. All five conversions refuse a negative count now; the GATE still answers. (3) DELIBERATE AND PINNED -- and this is the conflict ITEM 3 asked for: tests/test_derive.py has ALREADY landed `accum_due(Backwards(52), 0) is True`, `(Backwards(52), -4) is True` and `(Backwards(-4), 4) is False`, so making accum_due refuse would contradict three live assertions. I did not touch the behaviour. What I did fix is the attribution: the landed test comment credits the clamp to "accum_due's docstring" and accum_due's docstring said nothing about it -- the argument lived in opt_steps_from_backwards' docstring and in accum_due's own refusal message. accum_due's docstring now carries it, so the comment is true rather than the test being wrong. FOUR MORE FINDINGS FELL OUT OF READING THE ORACLE TABLE FIRST, as ITEM 3 asked: run_windows_from_epochs' NO FLOOR paragraph ended by calling opt_steps_from_windows' FLOOR a refusal, three lines after arguing a floor is not a refusal (measured: RUN_EPOCHS=0 -> Windows(0) -> Steps(1)); opt_steps_from_backwards' list of which siblings refuse a divisor below 1 said three and it is four; the same docstring's 'until it lands' sentence about the OPT guard is now landed; and the derive negative arm is now UNREACHABLE from src/ because counters() holds the only call and its guard fires one line earlier -- said in the docstring rather than left to be found. NOTHING WAS REMOVED OR DOWNGRADED: every new arm is a refusal added beside an existing one, and no assertion in the 575-case table or the landed smoke block moved. The schedule demonstration was re-run at all five configurations in fresh processes: shipped defaults, OPT_LR_SCHED=none (flat 0.002 at every step), OPT_BATCH_WINDOWS=16 OPT_ACCUM=4 (effective=64, horizon 15 steps), the P3-H29 shape (240 steps against 62 backwards, counters() raises), the clean case (52 backwards -> exactly 13 steps, opt.accum.invariant FIRED '52 backward // 4' vs 13) and the new guard (a 3-pass regression after a resume raises with all four numbers). Suite after: ownership 13 checks + 32 self-test cases 0 failing, contract 15 + 59 0, census 8 0, assemble 9 0, couplings 4 0, derive 575 oracle cases 0 mismatches, and tests/test_fabric.py 8 checks 0 failing -- its check_f8_manage_period_kind_and_refusal now stands over my refusal and names it in its own detail line.

findings.detail: ASYMMETRY (2), AND IT IS WIDER THAN FILED AND IT WAS LIVE. z_checks filed 'no negative guard at the count end of run_windows_from_epochs'. Re-measured across the whole family, the count end had THREE behaviours for one situation: opt_steps_from_backwards REFUSED a negative, run_windows_from_epochs PASSED IT THROUGH (Epochs(-1) x 10 -> Windows(-10)), and flush_period, flush_period_windows and opt_steps_from_windows FLOORED it -- flush_period(Steps(-100), 16) -> Flushes(1), flush_period_windows(Windows(-100), 16) -> Flushes(1), opt_steps_from_windows(Windows(-1024), 64) -> Steps(1). The floor is documented FOR A PERIOD THAT TRUNCATED TO ZERO ('One flush is the smallest cadence that exists'); applied to a negative it answers the TIGHTEST cadence in the system, which is the armed-but-inert class inverted into fires-every-flush. THIS ONE WAS REACHABLE AT BUILD TIME, not by direct call: `assemble.build({'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY': '-500'})` gave FAB.d_manage_period = Flushes(1), and `assemble.build({'CAP_PIN_WINDOWS': '-20000'})` gave FAB.d_cap_lift_period = TOK.d_cap_lift_period = Flushes(1) -- the management pass, the fabric cull, the spares, the replication and both cap lifts on EVERY flush of the run, from one negative env value, with the whole suite green. Nothing upstream bounds it: spine/lever.py::Lever takes (default, help, unit, choices) and has no range facility, and spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce resolves an int lever as `int(float(raw))`, which accepts '-500'. THE ASYMMETRY IS ACCIDENTAL AND THE PROOF IS IN THE SAME FUNCTION: its RATE end already refused its half of exactly this shape -- OPT_BATCH_WINDOWS=0 and =-4 both raise UnitError out of assemble.build today -- so one nonsense number stopped the build and the other silently became the fastest cadence in the system. FIXED at all five conversions, placed AFTER the rate checks for the order opt_steps_from_backwards already argues for (a bad rate makes every answer wrong rather than one), and the floor's `< 1` is kept and re-explained: with the count refused non-negative and the rate at or above one it can now only ever see a true zero, which is the only case its paragraph ever argued for. NO ORACLE ASSERTION MOVES: the landed table's clocks are all >= 0 and 575 cases + smoke still pass. tests/test_fabric.py::check_f8_manage_period_kind_and_refusal, added this round by another agent, now stands over this refusal and its detail line names it: 'at -5 the refusal came from the assembly (spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows, via the FAB.d_manage_period coupling)'.

unfinished.reason: tests/** is outside my grant (I own src/opt/api.py and src/spine/derive.py). Every assertion below was executed verbatim against the live tree in a fresh process and passes; none of them passes against the committed derive.py, which is the point.
unfinished.detail:
INSERT AFTER the line `    assert derive.accum_due(Backwards(52), 4) is True                       # 52 = 4 x 13, remainder 0` (occurs once, at tests/test_derive.py:418), i.e. at the end of the rate-end block and before the pin_tick paragraph. `Decimal` and `Fraction` are NOT needed; Fraction is already imported at the top of smoke().

    # THE RATE END IS A COUNT, AND `int()` WAS ADMITTING EVERYTHING int() ADMITS. The Clock
    # refusals above were half the hole: flush_period(Steps(20000), 16.9) answered Flushes(1250)
    # for a rate 6% off, '16' answered the same for a value that never went through
    # spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce, and nan and inf left through ValueError and OverflowError --
    # OUTSIDE the family's own exception type, which is the same escape units.py::Clock.convert
    # closed one layer down on 2026-09-04. A bool is refused for the reason the clock end
    # refuses True: bool is an int subclass and `type(x) is not int` is the exact-type shape.
    for fn, clk in ((derive.flush_period, Steps(20000)),
                    (derive.flush_period_windows, Windows(20000)),
                    (derive.opt_steps_from_windows, Windows(1024)),
                    (derive.opt_steps_from_backwards, Backwards(52)),
                    (derive.accum_due, Backwards(52))):
        for rate in (16.0, 16.9, '16', True, Fraction(33, 2), None,
                     float('nan'), float('inf')):
            try:
                fn(clk, rate)
                raise AssertionError(f"{fn.__name__} accepted {rate!r} as its rate")
            except UnitError:
                pass
    for rate in (10.0, '10', True, None):
        try:
            derive.run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(3), rate)
            raise AssertionError(f"run_windows_from_epochs accepted {rate!r} as its rate")
        except UnitError:
            pass

    # A NEGATIVE COUNT IS REFUSED BY ALL FIVE CONVERSIONS AND ANSWERED BY THE GATE. Until
    # 2026-09-05 only opt_steps_from_backwards refused: run_windows_from_epochs passed a
    # negative through and the other three FLOORED it to one -- the tightest cadence and the
    # shortest horizon that exist. Two of those were live at BUILD time through
    # spine/assemble.py::COUPLINGS (FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-500 built FAB.d_manage_period=Flushes(1)).
    for fn, bad, rate in ((derive.flush_period, Steps(-100), 16),
                          (derive.flush_period, Steps(-1), 1),
                          (derive.flush_period_windows, Windows(-100), 16),
                          (derive.opt_steps_from_windows, Windows(-1024), 64),
                          (derive.opt_steps_from_windows, Windows(-1), 1)):
        try:
            fn(bad, rate)
            raise AssertionError(f"{fn.__name__} accepted a negative count: {bad!r}")
        except UnitError:
            pass
    for n in (-1, -3, -634):
        try:
            derive.run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(n), 10)
            raise AssertionError(f"run_windows_from_epochs accepted Epochs({n})")
        except UnitError:
            pass
    # THE ZERO IS NOT THE NEGATIVE, and both floors that remain are the ones their docstrings
    # argue for: a cadence shorter than one flush, and a horizon that would divide by zero in
    # n_cycles. These four are the controls that keep the refusals above from being a blanket.
    assert derive.flush_period(Steps(8), 16) == Flushes(1)
    assert derive.flush_period_windows(Windows(8), 16) == Flushes(1)
    assert derive.opt_steps_from_windows(Windows(0), 64) == Steps(1)
    assert derive.run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(0), 10) == Windows(0)

NOTHING FAILS UNTIL IT LANDS -- the suite is green either way. What is missing is coverage: reverting any one of the six type tests or any one of the four new negative guards in src/spine/derive.py leaves tests/test_derive.py green today. PROVEN BY PLANT, not argued: I copied src/, tests/ and .rework/oracle/ to a scratch tree outside the repository, deleted flush_period_windows' negative guard there, and ran everything. tests/test_derive.py reported 575 oracle cases, 0 mismatches, smoke OK; tests/test_fabric.py reported 8 checks 0 failing with F8 still PASSING -- its detail line just moves to 'at -5 the refusal came from FAB.manage_period', because FAB's own REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD catches it at the read, so F8 alone does not hold this line. The block above, run against that same planted tree, FAILS with 'AssertionError: flush_period_windows accepted a negative count: Windows(-100)'. It is red on the plant and green on the tree, which is what makes it worth landing.
